title: Potential Rate Measurements for Uptake of Bicarbonate and Acetate by Microbes in Crustal Fluids
author: Julie Huber
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iutcewn

steps.title: Prepare Bicarbonate and Acetate Stocks
steps.instruction: Prepare sterile, anoxic stocks of bicarbonate and labeled acetate in an anaerobic chamber using acid-washed, sterile Balch tubes sealed with rubber stoppers and aluminum crimps.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 600mM bicarbonate solution (10:1 unlabeled:labeled) and add 175 uL to each tube (target final concentration: 5 mM DIC).
Prepare a 10mM acetate solution (10:1 unlabeled:labeled) and add 53 uL to each tube (target final concentration: 25 uM acetate).

steps.title: Distribute Fluid Samples
steps.instruction: Use acid-washed tubing and a Masterflex peristaltic pump with sterile needles to distribute ~20 mL of fluid into the pre-prepared Balch tubes.

substeps.instruction: Fill 3 sterile controls for each isotope (6 total) first using a disposable syringe filter, then discard the filter and fill the remaining tubes.
Process all DIC samples first, then switch tubing to process acetate samples.
Use an exit needle (the same exit needle can be used for the same time series).

steps.title: Add Hydrogen and Incubate
steps.instruction: Create an overlying atmosphere of 50% N2/50% H2 by adding ~2 bar hydrogen.

substeps.instruction: Set the regulator to 2 bar and insert the needle for 2 seconds (observing the dip in the regulator) then return to 2 bar.
Incubate at the appropriate temperature (Room Temperature, 30, 55, or 80 °C).
For RT/20, place in the main lab and record the temperature using a nearby thermometer if possible.

steps.title: Sample Headspace for Methane
steps.instruction: For DIC samples, sample the headspace for methane at the designated sacrifice time point.

substeps.instruction: Cool the tube to room temperature (e.g., using cool water); for 80ºC samples, allow up to 30 minutes.
Shake the tube vigorously for 1 minute.
Use a 10 mL syringe with a stopcock to equilibrate the headspace.
Close the stopcock, remove the syringe, record the gas volume, and inject into the GC to record the concentration.

steps.title: Extract Sample from Tube
steps.instruction: Remove the entire sample from the Balch tube using a 30 cc sterile syringe with a needle and an exit needle, ensuring all air bubbles are removed from the syringe.

steps.title: Filter Sample
steps.instruction: Filter the sample slowly using an acid-washed 25 mm syringe filter holder with a pre-combusted GF/F filter.

substeps.instruction: Attach the filter holder to the syringe and filter gently.
Monitor for leaks and record any occurrences on the sample sheet.

steps.title: Rinse and Dry Filters
steps.instruction: Clean and dry the filters for storage.

substeps.instruction: Rinse filters with 30 mL of 0.5M NaCl solution using a fresh syringe.
Use an air-filled 30 cc syringe to remove residual liquid.
Remove tape from the tube, place the filter into a 30 mm petri dish, and dry overnight at 55 °C.
Wrap in electrical tape and store dry at room temperature.

steps.title: Store for Analysis
steps.instruction: Once back on land, place the filters in a desiccator until analysis of biomass enrichment in the stable isotope facility.
